clue.text: Play with little cat after a change of heart

indicators.note: the heart is the central letter of the nine-letter phrase, and changing it swaps that one letter for another

parts.note: pygmy means very small, as in a pygmy hippo
a lion is one of the big cats

explanation.surface: A theatre piece featuring a small cat, once the writer had a change of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: PYGMY LION has nine letters; its heart, the fifth letter Y, is changed to A. PYGMALION is a play by George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's drama about Professor Higgins and Eliza Doolittle is a well-known stage work.

clue.text: With due deference to right horse

parts.note: pace, from Latin, is used before a name to mean with respect to someone who disagrees

explanation.surface: Politely acknowledging a correct choice of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacer is a horse trained to a lateral gait, especially in harness racing.

clue.text: Getting even, Craig settled score

indicators.note: the letters are settled into a new order, as dust settles into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Craig finally got his own back, settling an old score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settled score' reads as one phrase, but 'settled' rearranges EVEN plus CRAIG and 'score' alone is the definition; 'Getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A score, in the sense of an old score to settle, is a resentment or complaint held against someone.

clue.text: Reading University's accepted good grades initially — not unexpectedly

indicators.note: initially says these letters come at the start of the answer, ahead of the rest

parts.note: A is a top exam grade, so two of them are As

indicators.note: accepted means the word for reading takes in another letter inside itself

parts.note: a perusal is a careful reading
U is the usual abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Reading University admitted students with top grades, which surprised nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading looks like the town and its university, but it is the noun meaning a perusal; 'accepted' puts U inside PERUSAL to give PERUSUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as is normal or customary, which is what happens when nothing is unexpected.

clue.text: Heron is up the creek not far from the coast

indicators.note: up the creek means in trouble or messed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wading bird has gone up a tidal creek near the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore waters and fishing lie close to the shoreline rather than out at sea.

clue.text: Almost secure cover for one who's retired?

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost
to tie something is to fasten or secure it

explanation.surface: Something nearly safe protects a person who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests leaving work, but here it means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is the garment covering someone who has gone to bed for the night.

clue.text: Modellers may use this ointment endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for ointment is cut off

parts.note: balsam is a soothing resinous ointment

explanation.surface: Hobbyists who build models may apply a certain ointment over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light wood that model makers cut into aircraft and boat parts.

clue.text: Spike has doll that is missing

indicators.note: missing says the letters for that is are absent from the doll's name

parts.note: Barbie is the famous fashion doll
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A spiky toy doll has gone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a sharp backward-pointing point, like the spike on a fish-hook.

clue.text: Unattached and promiscuous

definitions.meaning: of a person, morally lax and having many casual partners

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both untethered and, of behaviour, sexually lax or immoral.

clue.text: Pennsylvania gunmen in suitable American gear

indicators.note: in places the two abbreviations inside the word for suitable

parts.note: apt means fitting or suitable
PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
US stands for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: Armed men from Pennsylvania wear appropriate American kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gunmen' suggests criminals, but RA is the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is equipment or gear needed for a particular task.

clue.text: Primate in church with young offender

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A monkey-like animal turns up in a church alongside a juvenile delinquent.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimpanzee is an African ape, one of the primates.

clue.text: Stripper from 12 Coronation Street?

parts.note: the answer at 12 across is a term of endearment, like honey or sweetheart
Coronation Street is a long-running British TV soap opera

explanation.surface: A striptease artist from a TV soap opera's cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripper' suggests a performer; it is a cleaning compound that strips paint. Coronation Street is Britain's longest-running TV soap opera.
explanation.definitionFit: This alkaline cleaning powder is used to strip or degrease paintwork before redecorating.

clue.text: Rhode Island has it as a coastal feature

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
it is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A US state possesses a feature of its coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' looks like a pronoun; in British bars 'gin and it' is gin with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Where a river meets the sea is a typical feature of a coastline.

clue.text: Treasure Island — finally shell-like

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word Island

parts.note: shell-like is British slang for an ear, as in a word in your shell-like

explanation.surface: Treasure Island, ending with something shaped like a seashell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treasure Island' reads as the novel, but Treasure is the definition, a beloved person.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a treasure means they are a precious, beloved person.

clue.text: Smart lawyer allowed dog to have lead removed

parts.note: legal means permitted by law

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, so the dog loses its opening letter

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound

explanation.surface: A clever lawyer permitted a dog to be let off its leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' suggests a dog's leash, but it is the leading letter of BEAGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal phrase describes a sharp, keen-eyed lawyer.

clue.text: German city provided backing with subtle skill

indicators.note: backing means the combined letters are read from right to left

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr, Germany
if means provided, as in provided that

explanation.surface: A German city backed the project with considerable delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reads as support, but it reverses ESSEN plus IF.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is delicate refinement or skill in handling a situation.

clue.text: Ghastly female? True!

parts.note: rightful means legitimate or true, as in the rightful heir

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in horror on confirming a woman is awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something dreadful, shocking or very unpleasant.

clue.text: It's glee that's out for a writer of sad stuff

indicators.note: something out is out of place, so the letters are disarranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Joy has disappeared for a poet of melancholy.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, so its author writes about sorrow.

clue.text: Insert cop's rank

indicators.note: rank, meaning foul or corrupt, signals that the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to fill in a policeman's grade on a form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' reads as grade, but also signals rearranging INSERT and COP; the whole clue then describes a police grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A police inspector holds a rank above sergeant in British forces.

clue.text: Rough one succeeding, grabbing contents of sack

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: grabbing means the word for succeeding holds the middle letters within it

parts.note: next means following or succeeding

indicators.note: contents of takes the inside letters of sack, dropping its ends

explanation.surface: A coarse person comes next, snatching what is in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough estimate is approximate, not precise.

clue.text: Provoke one making an effort to import goods

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so the trier brings the goods inside

parts.note: a trier is someone who tries hard
G stands for good, so two of them are goods

explanation.surface: A trader trying hard to bring goods into the country stirs things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off or provoke it.

clue.text: Charles Stuart's head is in the frame

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A portrait of Charles Stuart, the king, hangs in the frame.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Stuart suggests the Stuart king; the name is split, CHAS from Charles and S from Stuart's head. 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the supporting frame of a car or other structure.

clue.text: Untidy accumulation left in vessel

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left inside the vessel

parts.note: a cutter is a small sailing boat

explanation.surface: A mess of stuff has been abandoned on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Clutter is a disorderly heap of things lying about.

clue.text: A little means such a lot as an indication of holiness

indicators.note: a little of the following words means just part of them is taken, as a run inside

explanation.surface: Even a small amount can mean a great deal as a sign of saintliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' and 'as' are links; the letters run across 'suc-H A LO-t'.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is the ring of light shown around a saint's head in religious art.

clue.text: At it, on the 7

parts.note: 7 down means unattached; putting the word after At gives a phrase meaning free and roaming, the same as being on the run

explanation.walkthrough: The clue says 'at' plus the word means 'on the' plus 7 down, i.e. escaped and free.
explanation.definitionFit: At large and on the loose both describe someone escaped and roaming free.

clue.text: Front man judge listened to right away

parts.note: to figure is to reckon or judge

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is taken out of the word

parts.note: heard means listened to

explanation.surface: A presenter's verdict was heard and then dismissed at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as immediately, but means R is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurehead is a nominal leader, a front man without real power.

clue.text: End one's relationship with dyke

definitions.meaning: to dump or drop a partner
a trench dug to drain water

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to dump a partner and a trench for drainage.

clue.text: Man is one spreading lies

indicators.note: spreading lies suggests gossip, but here it scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A man is someone who goes around telling untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is a small island in the Irish Sea, so Man is an example.

clue.text: Prudence may be a relative of Soames, as reported

indicators.note: as reported means the word is spoken, so we want a sound-alike

parts.note: Soames is a character in Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga, so his relatives share his surname

explanation.surface: A woman named Prudence may be related to Soames, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prudence' looks like a woman's name; it is the definition, careful forethought. The Forsyte Saga is John Galsworthy's novel sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Planning ahead with care for the future is a form of prudence.

clue.text: Twig, for example, brought back by bird

indicators.note: brought back means the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A small branch, say, is carried back to its nest by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twig' looks like a branch; it is the informal verb meaning understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is British slang for to understand or catch on.

clue.text: Old master in Belgian city

definitions.meaning: a feudal lord to whom service was owed
a city in eastern Belgium on the Meuse

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a feudal superior and is also the French name of a Belgian city.

clue.text: There's an element such as yttrium? What a wonderful world!

parts.note: rare can mean excellent or wonderful, as in a rare treat
the earth is our world

explanation.surface: A chemist marvels at a lanthanide-group element and exclaims about the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Yttrium is one of the rare-earth metals grouped with the lanthanides.
